name: Diploma Animation & Multimedia
title: Diploma in Animation and Multimedia
intro: The animation and multimedia diploma roadmap: foundations, software, showreel and studio jobs.

phases.title: Class 10–12 and eligibility
phases.summary: Class 10 or 12 pass in any stream, depending on the course.
points: Diplomas are offered after Class 10 or Class 12 by polytechnics and private institutes.
Drawing and computer skills are helpful, but you can learn them in the course.
Watch animated films and study how characters move.
Build a small portfolio of sketches.

phases.title: Admission process
phases.summary: Institute entrance, portfolio review and interview.
points: Apply to polytechnics and institutes offering multimedia diplomas.
Some institutes conduct drawing or aptitude tests.
Check labs, software licences and placement record.
Confirm admission after fee payment.

phases.title: Foundation papers
points: Learn drawing, colour, design principles and storytelling.
Study the principles of animation and storyboarding.
Use graphic software like Photoshop and Illustrator.
Create short 2D animation exercises.

phases.title: Software and specialisation
points: Learn Maya or Blender for 3D, After Effects for motion graphics and Nuke for compositing.
Study video editing with Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve and sound basics.
Choose a specialisation: animation, modelling, VFX or multimedia design.
Produce a short film or project.

phases.title: Showreel and jobs
phases.summary: Build a showreel and apply to studios.
points: Create a short showreel of your best work.
Apply to animation studios, advertising agencies, gaming companies and media houses.
Roles: junior animator, video editor, motion graphics artist and multimedia designer.
Further study: B.Des, BSc Animation or specialised courses.
